title: Public Restrooms Near Me: Toilets on the Map
description: Find public restrooms near any place with Public Restrooms Near Me — toilets recorded in open map data, nearest pin first. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a family in an unfamiliar town centre gets the nearest recorded public toilet in seconds — a small tool that solves, as its intro says, a very real problem.
quick_answer: Public Restrooms Near Me shows the public toilets recorded in OpenStreetMap near a place you search or where you are heading. Search, press find, and head for the nearest pin — the restrooms the mapping community recorded, ranked by distance, for the moment no other geography matters.

faq: Are these guaranteed open?
No — the map records existence, not hours. Seasonal closures, locked evenings and maintenance happen. Treat the pin as the best lead, and venues like stations and libraries as the reliable backups.
Why is my town's restroom missing?
It may be unrecorded, or recorded after the data snapshot. OpenStreetMap improves exactly when locals add the facilities they know.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — search where you are heading instead; arguably the smarter use.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Facility records vary by source — councils list theirs, businesses theirs; the open map is the merged, imperfect picture.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
Accessible toilets specifically?
Where tagged with accessibility detail, the record shows it. The tagging is uneven — phone-ahead certainty belongs to the venue, discovery belongs to this map.
Baby-changing facilities?
Sometimes tagged, never guaranteed. The same rule: the pin starts the answer.
Does it work in rural areas?
Village public toilets are recorded where communities map them — trailheads and car parks are the usual rural pins.
Can I add one I know?
Yes — OpenStreetMap editing is open to all, and a toilet you add helps every traveller after you. The highest use of local knowledge there is.
Pay-to-use toilets?
Charged facilities exist in stations and some cities; where the record tags a fee, it shows — carry coins or a card in the classic European station case.
Night-time options?
24-hour venues (stations, services) are the night answer where recorded. The pin's existence plus the venue's hours, checked on the venue, is the complete plan.
